Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaClean Tech Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press * then 1 on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press * then 2. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaClean Tech's results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today's call are John Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Patel, Chief Financial Officer; and Tom Vargas, Chief Development Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Harlan.

John Harlan:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. NovaClean Tech delivered a solid performance in the Q2, driven by strong execution and growing demand for our renewable energy solutions. We are making significant progress on our strategic priorities, including expanding our project pipeline, enhancing our technological capabilities, and strengthening our partnerships.

I'd like to highlight four key aspects of our performance this quarter. First, let's review our overall performance highlights and key achievements. I'm excited to start our Q2 2024 earnings discussion with what has been an outstanding quarter for NovaClean Tech. As a frontrunner in comprehensive renewable energy offerings—from utility-scale solar photovoltaic systems, onshore and offshore wind farms, battery energy storage systems, and pioneering green hydrogen initiatives—we posted remarkable outcomes that demonstrate our operational prowess in a fast-changing clean technology environment.

Beginning with the headline figures, our total revenue hit $1.45 billion, a 28% jump from the prior year that exceeded our guidance midpoint by 12%. This represents our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit expansion, propelled by a 35% increase in our primary engineering, procurement, and construction segment to $980 million, thanks to completions in sought-after U.S. and European regions. Operations and maintenance services climbed 22% to $210 million, supported by our growing 15 GW portfolio under management, and our early-stage green hydrogen and long-duration storage initiatives added $60 million—the first substantial contributions from these lucrative areas.

Turning to profitability, adjusted EBITDA reached $385 million, delivering a solid 26.5% margin, which is 150 basis points better than last year and our best Q2 on record. This improvement stems from streamlined supply chains, where silicon wafer prices fell 18% year-over-year due to steadying polysilicon markets, and our proprietary NEXGEN bifacial TOPCon modules hit a fleet-average efficiency of 23.2%. Free cash flow shone at $290 million, a 40% year-over-year rise, allowing for $150 million in share buybacks and a $75 million dividend distribution, all while maintaining $2.1 billion in liquidity.

Standout accomplishments this quarter emphasize our forward momentum. We brought online 2.8 GW of fresh capacity across renewables: 1.9 GW solar in the U.S. Southwest, capitalizing on IRA 45X manufacturing credits from our new 5 GW Texas gigafactory, plus 900 MW onshore wind in the Midwest with 12-year power purchase agreements averaging $35 per MWh—under the EIA's 2025 levelized cost of energy forecast of $42 per MWh. Overseas, our 450 MW floating offshore wind farm off Portugal, developed with Orsted, launched with a 52% capacity factor in early runs, surpassing industry norms by 8 points via our VortexBlade turbine technology featuring wake steering.

In energy storage, we rolled out 1.2 GWh of BESS, highlighted by a 500 MWh four-hour system for a California utility using advanced LFP cells from our CATL collaboration. This puts us ahead of competitors like Fluence and Tesla in long-duration energy storage pursuits, with 92% cycle efficiencies and less than 1% degradation after 3,000 field-test cycles.

Geographically, North America drove 62% of revenue, boosted by $4.2 billion in fresh IRA-supported contracts, such as 1.5 GW colocation solar-plus-storage pacts with Amazon and Microsoft. Europe supplied 28%, aided by REPowerEU momentum; our 800 MW Polish wind project captured €1.1 billion in EU grants. The remainder came from APAC and Latin America, including a 600 MW solar EPC contract in India via the PM Surya Ghar program and our initial 50 MW electrolysis offtake in Brazil with Petrobras for green hydrogen.

On strategy, our $12.5 billion backlog grew 32% year-over-year at a 3.2x book-to-bill ratio, with 65% slated for 2025-2026. We've progressed our innovation pipeline, with perovskite-silicon tandem cells at 29.5% lab efficiency headed for 2026 commercialization, and debuted a $200 million venture capital fund backing cleantech ventures like solid-state battery pioneer QuantumScape. In ESG, we cut Scope 1 and 2 emissions 45% year-over-year through fully renewable-powered factories, securing an MSCI AAA rating and $1.8 billion in ESG-linked debt at 75 basis points over Treasuries.

We faced hurdles like 60-day permitting delays in the U.S. and 5% average selling price pressure from Chinese module surplus, but our U.S.-focused manufacturing advantage and 85% contracted backlog provide protection. Moving forward, we're lifting full-year guidance to revenue of $5.9-6.1 billion, representing 24% growth; EBITDA margins of 26-27%; and EPS of $3.85-4.00.

Simply put, Q2 confirms NovaClean Tech's role as the premier integrator as renewables beat fossil fuels in 90% of global markets according to Lazard's LCOE analysis version 17. We're driving the energy transition forward.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Rachel Patel to discuss our financial results in more detail, including debt levels and financing costs, tax equity and project-level financing, as well as our capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets.

Rachel Patel:
Thank you, John. As John highlighted, we had a strong financial performance in the Q2. Our revenue was $1.45 billion, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by increased project commissioning and higher energy production across our portfolio. Our gross margin was 28.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $420 million, primarily due to increased investments in research and development and sales and marketing. Our net income was $225 million, or $2.42 per share. We ended the quarter with $2.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance for revenue to $5.9-6.1 billion and earnings to reflect the strong momentum.

Let me provide more depth on our balance sheet, starting with debt levels and financing costs, which form a vital part of our capital framework in this capital-heavy renewable sector. Our methodical strategy for project finance—using non-recourse debt at assets and fine-tuning corporate leverage—backs our ambitious 15 GW solar and storage pipeline while upholding investment-grade standards.

Key metrics as of June 30: total gross debt at $5.2 billion, up 8% from $4.8 billion last year, mainly from $650 million in new construction loans for 1.2 GW additions in Texas and California. This covers $420 million in term loans for the Pecos Solar + Storage hybrid—our debut 500 MWac site merging bifacial PERC panels with 200 MWh BESS—and $230 million in bridges for Northeast ITC-qualified rooftops. Net debt, netting $450 million unrestricted cash, is $4.75 billion, yielding a 3.4x net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA ratio—within our 3.0x-4.0x goal and better than 3.6x at 2023-end.

By type, 72% or $3.75 billion is non-recourse project debt across 28 assets with 14-year average tenor. This encompasses $1.8 billion in tax equity flips under IRA-boosted ITC/PTC, monetizing 85% of credits at over 8% yields with partners like US Bancorp and KeyBank. Corporate debt is 28% or $1.45 billion: $750 million revolver (undrawn, $200 million accordion), $500 million green bonds due 2030, and $200 million sustainability notes linked to SBTi emissions goals.

Financing costs averaged 4.1% weighted, down 20 basis points sequentially, via refis during Fed pauses. Q2 interest expense was $52 million, or 14% of EBITDA, with cash interest at 3.8% after $300 million swaps hedging 70% floating exposure at SOFR +125 bps. 85% fixed below 4.0%, buffering 10-year Treasury rises to 4.2%. Peers like NextEra Energy Partners face 4.8%, but our green premium priced €300 million Eurobonds 30 bps under peers, fueled by REPowerEU-aligned European demand.

In the U.S. (85% capacity), IRA aids $1.1 billion DOE loans under 3% for Southwest projects akin to Gemini Solar in Arizona. Europe refis shaved 40 bps on €450 million UK wind via Deutsche Bank green loans for 2 GW onshore under Net-Zero Industry Act. APAC is 5%, targeting J-REITs for 300 MW floating solar with Japan GX funds.

Debt peaks at $6.0 billion mid-2025 on 3 GW CODs, but FFO-to-debt hits 14% in 2026 from 12%. Initiatives: $400 million forward swaps for sub-4.0% blends, $800 million 2025 refis on legacy debt; sale-leasebacks freeing $250 million for storage; perpetual green hybrids like Orsted's. Covenants solid at 2.8x fixed charge coverage vs. 1.75x mins, maturities post-2026.

In high-inflation LCOE solar-storage at $35-45/MWh, our 92% IG-rated debt edges independents like Clearway, prioritizing CPI PPAs and ERCOT/CAISO merchant, diversifying to insurers/pensions for 10-12% ROIC.

Next, on tax equity financing and project-level financing, core to scaling our 5.2 GW operating assets and 12 GW pipeline. These lower capital costs amid IRA boosts for solar, storage, and wind.

Tax equity pairs us with institutions—banks, insurers, hyperscalers—for ITC/PTC/Clean Electricity ITC shares via flips: 99% benefits to investor (6-8% IRR, e.g., JPMorgan) until flip to our 85/15 control.

Q2 closed $650 million across three, YTD $2.1 billion up 35%, funding 1.1 GW solar-storage like 450 MW Desert Bloom (70% ITC: 50% base +10% domestic +10% energy community) with a major bank and Google via Section 6418 transfers, expanding pools 40-50% per Lazard.

Southwest/ERCOT strong: $400 million pre-commits for 600 MW WindRose PTC at $27/MWh. Covers 40-50% CAPEX, WACC to 4.2% from 5.8% pre-IRA. 2025: $3.5 billion targets, eyeing offshore 45Y PTC.

Project-level non-recourse debt (40-50% CAPEX) post-equity: Q2 $1.4 billion construction-term for 800 MW Horizon Storage (SOFR+175 bps, Mizuho/DNB), matching 25-year APS PPA $42/MWh. €500 million EMTN green bonds at 3.25%. Northeast: $450 million ECA for 300 MW/1.2 GWh NY storage at L+140 bps on $85/MWh NYISO prices.

Hedged 80% floating; greenium 50-75 bps edge. LFP/CATL batteries for CAISO merchant, 95% DSCR. Blends accelerate 2.3 GW NTP YTD; diversifying to Brookfield/APG supports 15-20% IRRs, $800 million storage transfers ahead.

These fuel 25% GW growth 2025 at 4.5% costs, building resilient stacks.

Finally, on capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets, we're accelerating with our top-tier 52 GW pipeline—largest among independent clean tech players—per IEA Renewables 2024, renewables at 35% global adds.

2024 guidance reaffirmed at 5.2 GW net adds, +28% YoY: 3.8 GWdc solar, 1.0 GW onshore wind, 0.4 GWh BESS. H1 2.1 GW done; H2 2.0 GWdc Southwest solar on 700 MW ready sites, PPAs $28/MWh with Google/Microsoft.

2025 raised to 7.8-8.2 GW (+50-58%): 5.0 GWdc solar, 1.8 GW onshore wind, 0.8 GW offshore, 1.0 GWh BESS. N-type TOPCon at 24.5%, LFP hybrids for duck curve. 15% CAGR to 2027, BNEF $20/MWh solar LCOE.

U.S. 65% or 5.2 GW: $1.2 billion PTC/ITC transfers, 2.5 GW ERCOT, 1.5 GW PJM/SPP (1.2 GW Horizon agrivoltaic Q4 COD, 30% ITC+).

Europe 1.5 GW: 800 MW German offshore stake like Hornsea, €45/MWh CfD. APAC 0.8 GW: India SECI, Vietnam PDP8 at $0.22/Wp.

Pipeline: 52 GW ($60B revenue equiv): 15 GW construction (8 GW solar/4 GW wind/3 GWh storage, 70% PPAs >12% IRR); 20 GW advanced (10 GW U.S. hybrids w/8h vanadium from Invinity); 17 GW early (2 GW H2 electrolyzers $1.50/kg, 1.5 GW Taiwan floating).

Prioritizing 40% storage vs. 3-5% curtailment, 25% U.S. merchant; First Solar JV for 85% domestic. Mitigate queues (500 MW jumps post-FERC 2023), aluminum volatility w/ €2.5B bonds. 60% U.S., 25% Europe, 15% growth.

Now, I'll turn the call back to John for closing remarks.

John Harlan:
Thank you, Rachel. In closing, I am confident that NovaClean Tech is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of NEXGEN bifacial TOPCon modules on your project economics?

John Harlan:
Good morning, David. Absolutely, happy to elaborate. Our NEXGEN bifacial TOPCon modules have been transformative for project returns, achieving that record 23.2% fleet-wide efficiency we highlighted. This directly translates to lower levelized cost of energy— we've seen LCOE drop to under $30 per MWh in our U.S. Southwest deployments, well below the $35-42 benchmarks from EIA and Lazard. The bifacial design captures 20-30% more rear-side irradiance, boosting energy yield by 15% over monofacial PERC peers, which has allowed us to secure those attractive $35/MWh PPAs in the Midwest while maintaining 15-20% unlevered IRRs.

Supply chain optimization played a big role too—silicon costs down 18% year-over-year enabled tighter margins without sacrificing quality. In hybrids like Pecos Solar + Storage, the higher output pairs seamlessly with BESS for arbitrage, enhancing contracted revenues under IRA PTC/ITC stacks. Compared to legacy modules, NEXGEN reduces CAPEX by 8-10% per MW through higher power density—fewer panels, less BOS—and we've locked multi-year offtake with partners ensuring domestic content for full adders. Early pilots with tandems at 29.5% lab efficiency signal even more upside by 2026. Overall, this tech moat widens our edge in saturated markets like ERCOT and CAISO, supporting backlog conversion at superior economics. Rachel, anything to add on the financing side?

Rachel Patel:
Just quickly, David—the lower LCOE feeds directly into our debt service coverage, pushing DSCR north of 1.8x on recent facilities, which helped tighten spreads by 20-30 bps on project loans.

John Harlan:
Thanks, Rachel.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
Thanks. What are your expectations for grid connection timelines for your upcoming projects?

Tom Vargas:
Good morning, Lisa. Great question, as interconnection remains a key focus. With FERC Order 2023 reforms, we've seen cluster study backlogs shrink 20% across PJM and SPP, accelerating timelines from 3-4 years to 18-24 months for our shovel-ready queue. We've prioritized 700 MW in Arizona/Texas with executed queue positions and $1.2 billion in transferability proceeds to fast-track EPC. For the 2.0 GW H2 Southwest solar slated for H2 COD, we're on track for Q4 2024 grid-ups, leveraging 500 MW of 'ready-to-build' jumps.

In Europe, REPowerEU has streamlined permitting for our 1.5 GW 2025 adds, with the German North Sea offshore at 12 months post-FID thanks to CfD auctions. Challenges like U.S. permitting delays—averaging 60 extra days—persist, but 85% contracted backlog and storage co-location mitigate risks. We've hedged with 15 GW under construction all queued for end-2025 CODs, and early-stage 17 GW benefits from TLP platforms in Taiwan cutting floaters to 24 months. Overall, expect 90% of 2025 guidance within original timelines, supported by Bechtel partnerships and domestic manufacturing compliance.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to John Harlan for any closing remarks.

John Harlan:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in NovaClean Tech. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
